prize_parts.citation: For the prediction of flat electronic bands at the magic twist angle in bilayer graphene and the experimental discovery of correlated insulating and superconducting states in twisted bilayer graphene

statement.case_for: I keep twisted bilayer graphene as my single-part choice, with the same three names. After round 1 the case rests on three things that the discussion has not weakened. First, the structure is a prediction followed by an experiment in exactly the predicted regime: Bistritzer and MacDonald's continuum model gave nearly flat bands at a magic angle, and Jarillo-Herrero's group found correlated insulators and superconductivity there. Second, the phenomenology (flat bands, correlated insulating states, superconducting domes) has been reproduced by many groups with transport, scanning probes and spectroscopy, so the settled core is real even though the mechanism is not. Third, it created a tunable platform for strong correlations, which is a different kind of consequence from a better instrument. I would word the citation around the flat-band prediction and the observed correlated states and say nothing about pairing symmetry. My configuration is unchanged, but I have moved B043 to the first alternative because the round-1 exchange shows it is the best-supported fallback and I would vote for it without reluctance if the committee prefers a mature, cleanly attributed achievement. I have dropped B019 from my alternatives: I withdrew it as a preferred outcome in round 1 and my proximity to the method means I should not be the one carrying it.
statement.case_against: The objections I take most seriously are timing and credit. The experiments date from 2018, the origin of the superconductivity is open, and Danielsson, Johansson and Mehlig regard this as premature. Credit is also not tidy: Cao and Fatemi did the experiments, Dean's group established related hBN moire physics, and Lopes dos Santos, Peres and Castro Neto had an earlier continuum treatment of twisted bilayers. Under the three-person cap a part for B029 necessarily leaves out real contributors. Compared with the optical lattice clock, which has a two-name attribution that maps onto the concept and the record accuracy and which has been cross-checked between laboratories at the 1e-18 level, B029 is the less mature and less cleanly attributed case. If the committee judges that maturity and attribution should outweigh novelty this year, B043 is the defensible choice and I would not obstruct it.

responses.point: Danielsson now anchors on B043 and pairs it with IceCube credited to Halzen alone, while keeping B029 as a leading alternative to be revisited in a few years because the experiments date from 2018, the superconductivity is unresolved and the credit is untidy.
responses.response: The maturity point is the strongest argument against my choice and I do not dismiss it. I disagree on one thing: a citation limited to the flat bands and the correlated insulating and superconducting states does not depend on the mechanism, in the same way that the 1987 prize for high-temperature superconductivity did not wait for a pairing theory. I also doubt that pairing B043 with a one-name IceCube part improves on either achievement alone. You concede that a lone laureate for a collaboration of hundreds is the weak point, and I agree. If no clean credit exists, I would drop that half, as you suggest, and not stretch the cap to keep two parts.

responses.point: Mehlig prefers B008 (Kane, Mele, Molenkamp), argues that the 2016 prize did not cover time-reversal-invariant topological insulators, and holds that twisted bilayer graphene should wait until its mechanism is settled, though he is open to moving it up.
responses.response: I find his answer on the 2016 overlap convincing: the quantum spin Hall effect and the Z2 invariant are a distinct principle with their own experimental confirmation, so I rank B008 as a real alternative and I thank him for correcting my earlier worry. Where we still differ is on timing. Fifteen to twenty years of confirmation makes B008 more mature, but the Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang proposal that guided the HgTe experiment is not covered by Kane, Mele and Molenkamp, and it is the same kind of credit gap as I accept for B029 with Cao, Fatemi and Lopes dos Santos. I would not call one clean and the other untidy. On the mechanism I am answering his objection as in round 1: the citation is for the flat-band prediction and the observed correlated states, and I would not advocate it if it needed to say why the superconductivity occurs.

responses.point: Kroll argues that the lattice clock rests on the magic-wavelength concept, which removes the trade-off between trapping atoms and perturbing the transition, that it is distinct from the 2005 and 2012 prizes, and that it is mature and widely reproduced, while saying he would not block a condensed-matter discovery this year.
responses.response: I accept the distinction from the comb and from single-ion control; the magic-wavelength condition is a concept and not only a refinement, and I now regard B043 as the strongest fallback in the room. My remaining hesitation is the one he states himself: the gain is an instrument-enabled improvement in measurement, and no new physics has yet come out of it. That is not an objection to quality, only to how much weight a physics prize should put on the category. I would not delay B043 for the redefinition of the second, and I agree with his and Lindroth's view that demonstrated performance is what is being rewarded.

responses.point: Olsson asked how a DMFT citation would be worded and which phenomenon it would name, and said she would not put a method above an achievement that created a new experimental platform; she holds B029 first but concedes that the maturity gap is the real argument for the clock.
responses.response: She is right that a DMFT citation would have to name a method, and I have no phenomenon-based wording that would satisfy the criterion better than twisted graphene does; that is part of why I stepped back. On her handling of Cao and Fatemi, I think the three-name cap forces us to credit the group leader and the originator of the idea, as the committee normally does, and to say in the citation that the discovery is of the states, not of one device. I share her concession on maturity. We both think the clock is the stronger case on confirmation and attribution, and the choice between it and B029 is a judgement of what the prize should recognise, which I make in favour of the new regime but could be outvoted on without objection.

responses.point: Pearce anchors his configuration on B043 and credits Halzen alone for IceCube, arguing that a collaboration of hundreds should be reduced to the intellectual leader, and keeps B029 and B008 as alternatives because of unresolved superconductivity and credit.
responses.response: I agree with him on B008 and B029 as the pair of condensed-matter alternatives, and on the scientific significance of the IceCube diffuse flux. On attribution I cannot see how a single name is defensible. He describes Halzen as originator of the concept and scientific case, but the discovery also depended on detector construction and analysis leadership, and he himself admits Karle and Yoshida have claims. A single credit in a two-part prize in which the other part has two laureates would look arbitrary to the neutrino community. I would rather see the committee settle on one coherent achievement than adopt a two-part prize that exists mainly to fit the cap.

uncertainties: Whether the committee accepts a citation that names the flat-band prediction and the correlated insulating and superconducting states without the mechanism, and whether Danielsson, Johansson and Mehlig regard that as mature enough this year.

Whether the three-name cap can fairly handle Cao, Fatemi, Dean and the earlier Lopes dos Santos, Peres and Castro Neto work, or whether this is better served by a configuration with a cleaner attribution such as B043.
Whether the committee views the optical lattice clock as a discovery or as measurement science, which decides whether my fallback is also the better choice.
I rely on the supplied round-1 statements and general knowledge, not independent verification, for the IceCube and gamma-ray burst credit histories, on which I defer to the astroparticle members.
statement.conflict_note: No personal or institutional connection to Bistritzer, MacDonald or Jarillo-Herrero is apparent from my profile. I have field proximity to DFT, moire band-structure calculations and DMFT, and I disclosed in round 1 that I would consider recusing from a DMFT-centred part; I no longer advocate B019 and it is not in my configuration or alternatives. I see no connection to Katori, Ye or the other shortlisted candidates, and the other members' disclosures (Johansson on circuit QED, Kroll and Olsson on B043) do not affect the configuration I propose.
